endpoints.name: Collaboration Whitelist
endpoints.description: The external domains this enterprise permits collaboration with, and the direction each is allowed in. When entries exist, collaboration with any other domain is blocked -- so this is the explanation for invitations that silently fail, and the boundary of who can be shared with at all.

endpoints.name: Collaboration Whitelist Entry
endpoints.description: One allowed domain entry by id.

endpoints.name: Collaboration Whitelist Exempt Targets
endpoints.description: The users exempted from the domain restrictions. Every row here is someone who can share outside the permitted domains, which makes this a short and important list for an access review.

endpoints.name: Collaboration Whitelist Exempt Target
endpoints.description: One exempt user by id.

endpoints.name: Collaboration
endpoints.description: One collaboration by id: who was granted access to which file or folder, the ROLE they hold, the status, who invited them and when, and any expiry. Roles run editor, viewer, previewer, uploader, previewer uploader, viewer uploader, co-owner and owner -- the distinction that matters most is that anything from editor upward can change or remove content.

endpoints.name: File Collaborations
endpoints.description: Everyone with explicit access to one file, with their role and status. Requires a file id. Note it lists collaborations granted ON THIS FILE; access inherited from a parent folder does not appear here, so an empty result does not mean the file is private.

endpoints.name: Folder Collaborations
endpoints.description: Everyone with explicit access to one folder, with role and status. Requires a folder id. Because access is normally granted at folder level and inherited downward, this is where sharing actually lives -- and where an external collaborator on a whole tree shows up.

endpoints.name: Pending Collaborations
endpoints.description: READ THE NAME LITERALLY: this returns ONLY collaborations awaiting the caller's acceptance, not the account's collaborations. Box has no endpoint that lists every collaboration -- they are reachable per file or per folder, so an access review has to walk the content tree. Treating this as the sharing table understates access to almost nothing.

endpoints.name: Group Collaborations
endpoints.description: The folders and files one group has been granted access to, with the role on each. Requires a group id. The reverse view: what a team can reach, rather than who can reach one item.

endpoints.name: Collections
endpoints.description: The calling user's collections -- in practice the Favorites collection, which is the only type Box currently supports. Scoped to the caller.

endpoints.name: Collection Items
endpoints.description: The items in one collection. Requires a collection id. Same fields rule as folder items.

endpoints.name: File Comments
endpoints.description: The comments left on one file, with the message, the author and when it was posted. Requires a file id. Where discussion about a document lives; the file record carries no indication that any exists.

endpoints.name: Comment
endpoints.description: One comment by id, with its message and author.

endpoints.name: Device Pin
endpoints.description: One device pin by id.

endpoints.name: Enterprise Device Pins
endpoints.description: The mobile devices authorised for the enterprise, with the user, device name and platform. Requires an enterprise id. A device inventory: it shows which endpoints hold synced content, which no user or file table reveals.

endpoints.name: Download File
endpoints.description: The binary contents of one file. Requires a file id. NOT tabular data -- it returns the file itself, or a redirect to it, so it is useful for retrieving a document and useless for reporting on one.

endpoints.name: User's Email Aliases
endpoints.description: The additional email addresses registered to one user. Requires a user id. Relevant because collaborations and events can reference any of them, so matching activity to a person by primary email alone misses some of it.

endpoints.name: User and Enterprise Events
endpoints.description: The event stream of the account -- who did what to which item and when. TWO DIFFERENT STREAMS come from this one endpoint and the stream_type parameter chooses between them. The user stream returns the calling user's own recent activity. The ADMIN LOGS stream returns enterprise-wide events -- logins, downloads, shares, deletions, permission changes -- and is the audit trail an access or compliance question needs; it requires admin credentials. Two limits worth stating: the enterprise stream is not real time and lags by a period Box does not guarantee, and history is bounded by the retention Box keeps for the account, so questions about long-past activity may find nothing rather than an empty answer.

endpoints.name: File Version Legal Hold
endpoints.description: One file version legal hold record by id.

endpoints.name: File Version Legal Holds
endpoints.description: The individual file versions frozen by legal holds, one row each, with the hold that froze them. Filter by a legal hold policy assignment. This is the version-level record of what is actually under hold -- the assignment says what a hold reaches, this says which specific versions it caught, which matters because a hold placed on a user or folder pulls in versions nobody named.

endpoints.name: Retention on File
endpoints.description: One file version retention record by id.

endpoints.name: File Version Retentions
endpoints.description: The individual file versions currently held under retention, with the applicable policy and the disposition date. The record of what is actually retained, as opposed to what the policies say should be -- and the way to find what is due for disposition.

endpoints.name: File Versions
endpoints.description: The version history of one file, one row per prior version, with the version id, size, who created it, and when it was uploaded or restored. Requires a file id. NOTE that the CURRENT version is not among them -- this lists previous versions only, so a file never revised returns an empty list rather than one row. Storage questions want this: a heavily revised file consumes the sum of its versions, not the size shown on the file.

endpoints.name: File Version
endpoints.description: One prior version of a file by version id. Requires the file id as well.

endpoints.name: File Information
endpoints.description: One file's metadata. Requires a file id. Can carry name, size in bytes, created_at and modified_at, created_by, modified_by and owned_by, the parent folder, path_collection giving its full ancestry, sha1, item_status, and any shared link. Subject to the same fields rule as everything else here -- ask for what is needed by name or most of that list does not arrive. path_collection is the only place a file's full path exists; the record otherwise names just its immediate parent.

endpoints.name: Folder Information
endpoints.description: One folder's metadata, with the same shape as a file plus item counts and, when requested, size roll-ups. Requires a folder id, where 0 is the root. Same fields rule.

endpoints.name: Folder Items
endpoints.description: The direct contents of one folder -- files, subfolders and web links -- one row each, told apart by the type column. Requires a folder id, and FOLDER ID 0 IS THE ROOT of the account. This is the workhorse of the whole connector, because BOX HAS NO ENDPOINT THAT LISTS ALL FILES: content is reached by walking this folder by folder from the root, or by Search for Content. Two things decide whether the rows are usable. THE fields PARAMETER IS ALMOST ALWAYS REQUIRED -- Box returns a minimal record by default, carrying little more than type, id, name and etag, so size, timestamps, owner and parent are ABSENT unless asked for by name, and their absence looks like empty data rather than an unmade request. And large folders must be paged with marker rather than offset: pass usemarker=true, since offset paging is capped and silently stops.

endpoints.name: User's Groups
endpoints.description: The groups one user belongs to. Requires a user id. The per-person view of group-derived access, which no collaboration table gives.

endpoints.name: Group Members
endpoints.description: The members of one group, as membership records carrying the user and their role in the group. Requires a group id.

endpoints.name: Group Membership
endpoints.description: One group membership by id, with the user, the group and the role.

endpoints.name: Enterprise Groups
endpoints.description: The groups defined in the enterprise, with name, and the settings governing who may view members and invite them. Groups are how access is granted at scale, so this is the dimension that explains permissions no individual collaboration records.

endpoints.name: Group
endpoints.description: One group by id, with its settings.

endpoints.name: User Invite Status
endpoints.description: The state of one invitation to join the enterprise. Requires an invite id. Pending onboarding, which the user list does not show.

endpoints.name: Legal Hold Policies
endpoints.description: The legal holds in force, each with its name, description, and the period it covers. A legal hold freezes content against deletion regardless of retention policy, so anything under hold is exempt from the normal lifecycle -- which is why deletion counts and storage figures can behave unexpectedly during litigation.

endpoints.name: Legal Hold Policy
endpoints.description: One legal hold policy by id, with counts of its assignments.

endpoints.name: Legal Hold Policy Assignments
endpoints.description: What one hold applies to -- users, folders or files. Requires a policy id. The scope of the freeze.

endpoints.name: Legal Hold Policy Assignment
endpoints.description: One legal hold assignment by id.

endpoints.name: Current File Versions
endpoints.description: The files whose CURRENT version is held under one legal hold assignment. Requires an assignment id. What is frozen as it stands today.

endpoints.name: Previous File Versions
endpoints.description: The PRIOR versions held under one legal hold assignment. Requires an assignment id. Held separately from current versions because a hold preserves the history as well as the present state, and the two lists rarely match.

endpoints.name: Metadata Cascade Policies
endpoints.description: The policies that push a folder's metadata down onto everything inside it. Requires a folder id. Explains metadata appearing on files nobody set it on -- without this, inherited values look like they were applied individually.

endpoints.name: Metadata Cascade Policy
endpoints.description: One cascade policy by id.

endpoints.name: File Metadata Instances
endpoints.description: All metadata attached to one file, one entry per template applied. Requires a file id. Box metadata is how organisations record business attributes files do not natively have -- contract value, department, retention class. The VALUES ARE KEYED BY TEMPLATE FIELD KEY, so they cannot be read without the template: Metadata Template by Name or by ID is the decoder.

endpoints.name: File Metadata Instance
endpoints.description: One metadata instance on a file, identified by its scope and template key. Requires the file id, scope (enterprise or global) and template key.

endpoints.name: Folder Metadata Instances
endpoints.description: All metadata attached to one folder. Requires a folder id. Same keying, same need for the template.

endpoints.name: Folder Metadata Instance
endpoints.description: One metadata instance on a folder, by scope and template key.

endpoints.name: Metadata Template by Instance ID
endpoints.description: The template behind a given metadata instance id. The reverse lookup, for when an instance is in hand and its shape is not.

endpoints.name: Metadata Template by Name
endpoints.description: One metadata template by its scope and template key, with every field it defines: the field key, its display name, its type, and for enum fields the allowed options. THE DECODER for metadata instances -- an instance returns values under field keys and nothing else identifies them.

endpoints.name: Metadata Template by ID
endpoints.description: The same template found by its id rather than by name.

endpoints.name: Global Templates
endpoints.description: The metadata templates Box provides to every account, chiefly the properties template used for arbitrary key-value pairs. Reference data, identical everywhere.

endpoints.name: Enterprise Templates
endpoints.description: Every metadata template defined by this enterprise, with their fields. The account's own vocabulary for describing content, and the natural starting point before reading any metadata.

endpoints.name: Recently Accessed Items
endpoints.description: The items the calling user has recently opened, with the interaction type and time. Scoped to the caller, so it describes one person's activity rather than the account's.

endpoints.name: Retention Policies
endpoints.description: The retention policies defined in the enterprise, with the name, the retention length, the disposition action, and whether the policy is finite or indefinite. Retention decides how long content survives deletion, so this is what explains why some files cannot be removed and others vanish on schedule.

endpoints.name: Retention Policy
endpoints.description: One retention policy by id.

endpoints.name: Retention Policy Assignments
endpoints.description: What one policy applies to -- an enterprise, a folder, or a metadata template. Requires a policy id. The policy says the rule; this says its reach, and a policy assigned to nothing has no effect at all.

endpoints.name: Retention Policy Assignment
endpoints.description: One retention policy assignment by id.

endpoints.name: Search for Content
endpoints.description: Searches the account's content by keyword, with filters for file extension, size range, date range, owner, ancestor folder and content type. The alternative to walking the folder tree, and usually the faster route to a set of files. Note that search indexes content and metadata, is eventually consistent so very recent uploads may be missing, and returns trashed items only when explicitly asked for.

endpoints.name: Find Item for Shared Link
endpoints.description: Resolves a shared link URL back to the item it points at. Requires the link in a header rather than the path. Use it to identify what a circulating link actually exposes.

endpoints.name: Storage Policies
endpoints.description: The storage policies available to the enterprise, which determine the geographic region content is stored in. Data-residency configuration -- relevant to compliance questions about where content physically lives.

endpoints.name: Storage Policy
endpoints.description: One storage policy by id.

endpoints.name: Storage Policy Assignments
endpoints.description: Which users or enterprises each storage policy is assigned to. The reach of a residency rule.

endpoints.name: Storage Policy Assignment
endpoints.description: One storage policy assignment by id.

endpoints.name: Task Assignments
endpoints.description: Who a task was assigned to, with each assignee's resolution state and when they responded. Requires a task id. The task says what was asked; this says who answered and how.

endpoints.name: Task Assignment
endpoints.description: One task assignment by id.

endpoints.name: Tasks on File
endpoints.description: The review or approval tasks attached to one file, with the action required, the message, the due date, and the completion rule. Requires a file id. Box tasks are how a document is routed for approval, so this plus its assignments is the audit of who was asked to sign off.

endpoints.name: Task
endpoints.description: One task by id, with its assignments and completion state.

endpoints.name: Terms of Services
endpoints.description: The terms of service configured for the enterprise, with their text, whether each is enabled, and whether it applies to managed users or to external collaborators. Configuration.

endpoints.name: Terms of Service
endpoints.description: One terms of service by id.

endpoints.name: Terms of Service User Statuses
endpoints.description: Who has accepted a given terms of service and when. Requires a terms of service id. The acceptance record, and therefore the compliance evidence -- the policy alone proves nothing about uptake.

endpoints.name: Trashed File
endpoints.description: One trashed file's metadata by file id. Confirms an item is in the trash and reports when it was deleted; a file not in the trash is not found here.

endpoints.name: Trashed Folder
endpoints.description: One trashed folder's metadata by folder id.

endpoints.name: Trashed Items
endpoints.description: Everything currently in the account's trash -- files, folders and web links -- with when each was moved there. Deleted content is EXCLUDED from Folder Items and from search, so a count taken there does not include it; this is where it went. Items leave trash permanently after the retention period, so this is a window, not a history.

endpoints.name: Trashed Web Link
endpoints.description: One trashed web link by id.

endpoints.name: Upload Session
endpoints.description: The state of one chunked upload in progress, with the total parts expected and how many have arrived. Requires a session id. Operational, and short-lived -- it describes an upload happening now, not any file that exists.

endpoints.name: Upload Session Parts
endpoints.description: The parts already uploaded in one chunked session, with their offsets and sizes. Requires a session id. Same short-lived scope.

endpoints.name: Enterprise Users
endpoints.description: The user accounts in the enterprise, one row each. Carries name, login, status (active, inactive, cannot delete or edit, and so on), role, created_at, and -- when requested by name -- SPACE_AMOUNT and SPACE_USED in bytes. Those two are the storage-per-user answer and are among the fields Box omits unless the fields parameter asks for them. Note that inactive users still own their content, so excluding them from a storage total loses that content rather than tidying the figure.

endpoints.name: Current User
endpoints.description: The account the credentials belong to. One record, always the caller -- and worth reading first, because most listings here are scoped to what this user can see, and an admin token and a user token return very different pictures of the same account.

endpoints.name: User
endpoints.description: One user by id. Same fields and the same fields-parameter rule.

endpoints.name: File Watermark
endpoints.description: Whether a watermark is applied to one file, and when it was set. Requires a file id. A protection setting; its presence usually indicates content the business treats as sensitive.

endpoints.name: Folder Watermark
endpoints.description: Whether a watermark is applied to one folder, cascading to its contents. Requires a folder id.

endpoints.name: Web Link
endpoints.description: One web link by id -- a bookmark stored in the folder tree alongside files, with its url, name and parent folder. Web links appear as rows in Folder Items and are neither files nor folders, so a naive file count that does not filter on type includes them.

endpoints.name: Webhooks
endpoints.description: The webhooks configured on the account: the item each watches, the events it fires on, and its target URL. Integration configuration; deliveries are not recorded here. Worth checking to see whether an external system already receives this content in real time.

endpoints.name: Webhook
endpoints.description: One webhook by id.
